title: Homo neanderthalensis (Neanderthals)
summary: Neanderthals were a distinct species of archaic human who lived across Europe and southwestern to central Asia from about 400,000 to 40,000 years ago. Short, stocky and cold-adapted, they made Mousterian stone tools, controlled fire and buried their dead, and some of their DNA survives in people today.

uncertainty.note: Both sources round to "about 400,000 to 40,000 years ago"; the figures are used as years and not converted from before-present counts. The Natural History Museum says the best-known Neanderthals lived 130,000 to 40,000 years ago.

where.modern_name: Neander Valley, Germany (type locality; the species ranged across Europe and southwestern to central Asia)
where.historical_name: Neander Valley near Mettmann; species range Europe to the Altai, no polities

importance.justification: The best-studied extinct human relative and a source of DNA in living people.
